used.how: the flat op takes the stored [N, K] matrices laid out tile-transposed (weights_nk) and transposes in1 in its matmuls, so bfp8 groups run along K and stay exact; _load_block's _bfp8_exact on [N, K] covers the same 16-value groups, so the op's own load-time check is off
the routing weight still travels as three bf16 pieces in the dispatched row; _routing_rows sums them by one selector matmul into the op's Float32 routing_weights [rows, 32]
the selector matmul is exact by one product per tile-dot; the fork's exactness test uses selection gate / up weights (one power of two per output) so the device GEMMs are exact
test_ds41_h_options.py (flat fork) checks the in-kernel quant bit for bit on exact GEMMs (identity down), negative controls incl. per-half scales
the flat SFPU steps (se_rh.hpp) keep unified's two-pass structure: h *= r first for every h tile, then the quant with s / 1/s parked in the consumed weight tile
the routing-weight tile and the exchanged fp32 halves unpack straight into the fp32 DEST (UnpackToDestFp32), never through SrcA at TF32

rh_quant reproduces tt/quant.fp8_qdq's arithmetic (clamp 1e-4, fp32(1/448), ue8m0 from the bits, e4m3 RNE on the integer bits, subnormal step 2^-9)
